svg.text: Two solves of the same corner, differing only in the length of the straight that follows. Distance along the track runs left to right in every panel; the shaded band is the corner.
30 m of straight after the corner:
5.83 s over 163 m · apex 49% through the corner · slowest 24.6 m/s · exit 27.5 m/s · worst slip 12.0° · envelope violations 0.0% · Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded
260 m of straight after the corner:
11.96 s over 393 m · apex 55% through the corner · slowest 24.3 m/s · exit 46.5 m/s · worst slip 12.0° · envelope violations 0.0% · Solve_Succeeded
Absolute times are not comparable between the two — they cover different distances. The comparable quantity is where the apex sits, and the shape of the speed trace through the corner.
[MEASURED] bicycle model + optimal control + Sedan_Pac02Tire.tir · offsets removed · m 1360 kg · 54% front · 200 nodes, 0.82 m apart · [SOURCED] RV-1 parameters §1
Slip angles constrained to ±12°, our imposed bound; the solver sits on that constraint through the corner, which is what a minimum-time answer should do.
